key_insight: You can compress long videos to a single, highly informative token per selected frame at the final LLM layer without losing essential temporal cues, enabling extreme reduction in token budget while preserving video-level understanding.
problem_solved: Addresses the scalability bottleneck of vision–language models for long videos, where per-frame token explosion exceeds LLM context length and forces sparse, temporally fragmented perception.
method: Highly selective frame selection: score and pick only the most informative frames across the video (learned or heuristic) to represent key moments.

Per-frame extreme compression: aggregate each selected frame into a single compact token using a learnable pooling/encoder (e.g., cross-attention or projection) that preserves semantics and temporal cues.

LLM integration with temporal priors: feed the one-token-per-frame sequence into the LLM with positional/temporal encoding and training objectives (distillation/contrastive) to retain temporal reasoning despite the slim token budget.
impact: Greatly lowers compute and memory costs for long-video VLMs, enabling practical LLM-based reasoning over hours of footage and broader deployment for tasks like summarization, retrieval, and long-term action understanding.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dense frames → selective frame scorer → one-token-per-frame compressor → LLM, showing token-count reduction
Bar chart: tokens (or FLOPs) vs accuracy/latency comparing full-frame, sparse sampling, and one-token-per-frame
Timeline visualization: original video timeline with highlighted selected frames and preserved temporal order
Icon set: clock/GPU for efficiency, token compression icon, and an LLM/head for downstream reasoning
paper_title: One Token per Highly Selective Frame: Towards Extreme Compression for Long Video Understanding
paper_authors: Zheyu Zhang, Ziqi Pang, Shixing Chen, Xiang Hao, Vimal Bhat
